subject: Logic
title: A Brief History of Fallacies
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: A Brief History of Fallacies.

hook.text: Twenty-three centuries ago, Aristotle wrote the first catalog of bad arguments. We're still adding to it.

buildup.text: In Sophistical Refutations, Aristotle listed thirteen fallacies used by Greek debaters to win unfairly.

discovery.text: Medieval scholars expanded the list. The Enlightenment made fallacy detection central to philosophy.

twist.text: Today, social media has become the world's largest fallacy laboratory—billions of arguments, mostly flawed.

climax.text: The names change, but the patterns repeat. Humans make the same reasoning errors across every era.

quiz.question: Who wrote the first known catalog of fallacies?
